answer: Die fingerprints: (1) each identity enrolls one PUF die, and a verifier replays 64 random challenges against the pattern enrolled once, a signature of that die's own dune of noise. (2) Two identities whose response sets correlate above 0.97, or one die answering for two keys, are voided and their $300 bonds slashed. (3) A counterfeit die costs $6 plus $14 test, so 5,000 fakes cost $100,000 and eight weeks at a foundry. An honest operator buys one chip, an ember kept lit; a farm pays per fake, and any thread of shared noise voids both. Paper is a shadow; a die's noise is a fingerprint.
